PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Maternal Age: 34 years
Gestation: 21 weeks
Indication for Testing: Advanced maternal age, chromosomal abnormality screening
Procedure: Amniocentesis

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Rapid aneuploidy screening for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from uncultured amniocytes obtained from 20ml of amniotic fluid. QF-PCR analysis was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers specific to chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. A minimum of four informative markers were analyzed per chromosome. Peak area ratios were calculated for all heterozygous markers. Normal diallelic ratios range from 0.8 to 1.4. Triallelic patterns or skewed ratios outside the normal range indicate trisomy.

RESULTS

CHROMOSOME 13
Markers analyzed: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
All markers showed normal heterozygous patterns
Peak ratios within normal range (0.95-1.12)
Result: Normal female pattern for chromosome 13

CHROMOSOME 18
Markers analyzed: D18S391, D18S390, D18S535, D18S386
All markers showed normal heterozygous patterns
Peak ratios within normal range (0.89-1.08)
Result: Normal female pattern for chromosome 18

CHROMOSOME 21
Markers analyzed: D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1435, D21S1446
All markers showed normal heterozygous patterns
Peak ratios within normal range (0.91-1.15)
Result: Normal female pattern for chromosome 21

SEX CHROMOSOME MARKERS
AMELOGENIN: XX pattern confirmed
TAF9: Normal female pattern

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis shows a normal female chromosome complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), or trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) was detected in this sample.

LIMITATIONS
This test screens only for common aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y. It does not detect:
- Structural chromosome abnormalities
- Mosaicism below 20%
- Aneuploidies of other chromosomes
- Triploidy
- Maternal cell contamination cannot be excluded without comparative maternal sample

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full karyotype analysis of G-banded chromosomes from cultured amniocytes is recommended to follow. This comprehensive cytogenetic analysis will detect structural abnormalities and aneuploidies not covered by QF-PCR screening. Culture and analysis are in progress and will be reported separately.

REPORTED BY
[redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
Report Date: [redacted date]
